---- MODULE W4Od10m1p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS N, MaxCap

\* A token ring with one position per train grants exclusive turns to enter the block.
Trains == 1..N

VARIABLES occupants, queue, tokenPos, capacity

vars == <<occupants, queue, tokenPos, capacity>>

QueuedTrains == {queue[i] : i \in DOMAIN queue}

Init ==
  /\ occupants = {}
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ tokenPos = 1
  /\ capacity = 1

Request(t) ==
  /\ t \notin occupants
  /\ t \notin QueuedTrains
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, t)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupants, tokenPos, capacity>>

ReqAny == \E t \in Trains : Request(t)

PassToken ==
  /\ IF queue = <<>> THEN TRUE ELSE Head(queue) # tokenPos
  /\ tokenPos' = (tokenPos % N) + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupants, queue, capacity>>

GrantToken ==
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ Head(queue) = tokenPos
  /\ Cardinality(occupants) < capacity
  /\ occupants' = occupants \cup {Head(queue)}
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenPos, capacity>>

Release(t) ==
  /\ t \in occupants
  /\ occupants' = occupants \ {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, tokenPos, capacity>>

RelAny == \E t \in Trains : Release(t)

\* Capacity may change at runtime, but never below current occupancy.
AdjustCapacity ==
  /\ \E newCap \in 1..MaxCap :
       /\ newCap >= Cardinality(occupants)
       /\ capacity' = newCap
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occupants, queue, tokenPos>>

Next == ReqAny \/ GrantToken \/ RelAny \/ PassToken \/ AdjustCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(GrantToken) /\ WF_vars(PassToken) /\ WF_vars(RelAny)

\* CapacityMutex generalizes mutual exclusion: occupancy never exceeds current capacity.
CapacityMutex == Cardinality(occupants) <= capacity

\* Every train that queues for the block is eventually admitted.
RequestGranted == \A t \in Trains : (t \in QueuedTrains) ~> (t \in occupants)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  N = 3
  MaxCap = 2
INVARIANT CapacityMutex
PROPERTY RequestGranted
nl:
A subway signalling block system guards entry to a single critical track
block shared by a small fleet of trains. Admission is arbitrated by a token
ring: the ring has one position per train, a token pointer advances around
the ring, and a train waiting to enter the block may only be admitted while
it is both at the head of the waiting queue and currently pointed to by the
ring's token. The block's capacity is not fixed at one train for the whole
run: the signalling operator can raise or lower the block's admissible
occupancy at runtime (for example to allow a coupled short-formation move,
or to derate the block during degraded signalling), subject only to never
setting the new capacity below the number of trains presently inside the
block.

The system has five actions. Request: a train not already inside the block
and not already waiting joins the tail of the waiting queue. PassToken: when
the queue is empty, or the train at the head of the queue is not the train
currently pointed to by the ring's token, the token pointer advances to the
next ring position. GrantToken: when the train at the head of the queue is
the one currently pointed to by the ring's token and the block has spare
capacity, that train is admitted into the block and removed from the head of
the queue. Release: a train presently inside the block exits, freeing its
place. AdjustCapacity: the operator picks a new capacity between 1 and the
configured maximum, provided it is not lower than the number of trains
currently occupying the block.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of trains occupying
the critical block never exceeds the block's current (possibly
operator-adjusted) capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every train that joins the waiting queue for the block is
eventually admitted into the block.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od17m2p1t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participant, MaxTxn

VARIABLES phase, votes, crashed, record, txnId

vars == <<phase, votes, crashed, record, txnId>>

\* Two-phase commit over a shared baggage-routing record: the coordinator
\* opens a preparing round, collects a yes/no vote from every station, and
\* only commits the round's transaction id into the record once every
\* station voted yes. A station can crash silently instead of voting; the
\* invariant below checks that a commit never happens while a vote is
\* missing because of such a crash, so no station's implicit veto is lost.

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ votes = [p \in Participant |-> "none"]
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ record = 0
    /\ txnId = 0

Propose ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ txnId < MaxTxn
    /\ txnId' = txnId + 1
    /\ phase' = "preparing"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed, record>>

Vote(p) ==
    /\ phase = "preparing"
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ votes[p] = "none"
    /\ \E v \in {"yes", "no"} : votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, crashed, record, txnId>>

\* The twist: a station that has not yet voted can go silent instead of
\* casting an explicit no.
CrashSilently(p) ==
    /\ phase = "preparing"
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ votes[p] = "none"
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, record, txnId>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "preparing"
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ \A p \in Participant : votes[p] = "yes"
    /\ record' = txnId
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed, txnId>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "preparing"
    /\ (crashed # {} \/ \E p \in Participant : votes[p] = "no")
    /\ phase' = "aborted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed, record, txnId>>

ResetRound ==
    /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ votes' = [p \in Participant |-> "none"]
    /\ crashed' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, txnId>>

Next ==
    \/ Propose
    \/ \E p \in Participant : Vote(p)
    \/ \E p \in Participant : CrashSilently(p)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ ResetRound

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: a committed record was actually agreed by every station.
NoLostUpdates ==
    phase = "committed" =>
        /\ record = txnId
        /\ crashed = {}
        /\ \A p \in Participant : votes[p] = "yes"

================================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Participant = {p1, p2, p3}
    MaxTxn = 3
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport baggage router coordinates several handling stations (conveyor
junctions, scanners, and gate-transfer arms) that must jointly agree before
the shared baggage-routing record -- which flight a given bag is currently
assigned to -- is updated. The router itself acts as a two-phase-commit
coordinator: for each proposed reassignment it opens a preparing round with a
fresh transaction id and asks every station to vote yes or no on whether it
can safely apply the change. Only once every station has voted yes does the
coordinator commit, writing that round's transaction id into the shared
record. If any station votes no, the coordinator aborts the round and the
record keeps its previous value. The twist is that a station can crash
silently while a round is preparing: instead of voting no, it simply stops
responding and joins the round's crashed set. The coordinator must treat a
silent crash the same way it treats an explicit no vote -- it detects the
missing response and aborts the round rather than committing, because
committing while a station is silently down would apply an update that
station never actually agreed to, effectively losing that station's implicit
veto and corrupting the shared record. After a round finishes, whether
committed or aborted, every station's vote and crash status is cleared and
the coordinator returns to idle so the next reassignment can be proposed.
The system supports six actions: Propose (the idle coordinator opens a new
preparing round with the next transaction id, bounded by a fixed maximum
number of rounds), Vote (a station that has not crashed and has not yet
voted in the current round casts yes or no), CrashSilently (a station that
has not crashed and has not yet voted in the current round instead stops
responding and is added to the round's crashed set), Commit (the coordinator
applies the round's transaction id to the shared record once every station
has voted yes and none has crashed), Abort (the coordinator abandons the
round, leaving the shared record unchanged, once some station has voted no
or some station has crashed), and ResetRound (once a round has committed or
aborted, all votes and crash markers are cleared and the coordinator returns
to idle).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the coordinator reaches the committed phase, the
shared record equals that round's transaction id and every station had
actually voted yes with none having crashed silently, so a station's missing
response can never be silently treated as an agreed update.

---- MODULE W4Od5m3p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Capacity, QCap, N, MaxOverrides

Nodes == 1..N

VARIABLES leader, admitted, pending, overrideCount

vars == <<leader, admitted, pending, overrideCount>>

\* Leader election with failover: a matchmaker node holds `leader` (0 =
\* vacant) and gates ordinary admissions into the lobby. A crash sends
\* leader back to 0 until the next election picks a replacement. A
\* privileged admin can force an admission even while the lobby is
\* leaderless, but every admission -- ordinary or overridden -- is still
\* checked against the lobby's fixed Capacity, which is the invariant below.

Init ==
  /\ leader = 0
  /\ admitted = 0
  /\ pending = 0
  /\ overrideCount = 0

RequestJoin ==
  /\ pending < QCap
  /\ pending' = pending + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, admitted, overrideCount>>

ElectLeader ==
  /\ leader = 0
  /\ \E n \in Nodes : leader' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, pending, overrideCount>>

LeaderFail ==
  /\ leader # 0
  /\ leader' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<admitted, pending, overrideCount>>

LeaderAdmit ==
  /\ leader # 0
  /\ pending > 0
  /\ admitted < Capacity
  /\ admitted' = admitted + 1
  /\ pending' = pending - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, overrideCount>>

\* Twist: the admin override forces an admission from the queue even when
\* the lobby is leaderless, bypassing the leader gate -- but not the
\* capacity bound, which applies to this action exactly like LeaderAdmit.
AdminOverrideAdmit ==
  /\ pending > 0
  /\ admitted < Capacity
  /\ admitted' = admitted + 1
  /\ pending' = pending - 1
  /\ overrideCount' = IF overrideCount < MaxOverrides
                       THEN overrideCount + 1 ELSE overrideCount
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader>>

PlayerLeave ==
  /\ admitted > 0
  /\ admitted' = admitted - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, pending, overrideCount>>

Next == RequestJoin \/ ElectLeader \/ LeaderFail \/ LeaderAdmit
        \/ AdminOverrideAdmit \/ PlayerLeave

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(ElectLeader) /\ WF_vars(LeaderAdmit)
        /\ WF_vars(AdminOverrideAdmit) /\ WF_vars(PlayerLeave)

\* Safety: the lobby's admitted-player count never goes negative and never
\* exceeds the fixed Capacity, whether an admission came through the
\* elected leader or through the privileged admin override.
CapacityNeverExceeded ==
  /\ admitted >= 0
  /\ admitted <= Capacity

\* Liveness: after a leader failure the matchmaker does not stay leaderless
\* forever -- a new leader is eventually elected, restoring failover.
LeaderEventuallyElected == leader = 0 ~> leader # 0

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
  Capacity = 2
  QCap = 2
  N = 3
  MaxOverrides = 2
INVARIANT CapacityNeverExceeded
PROPERTY LeaderEventuallyElected
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker runs a small pool of matchmaker nodes
that elect one of themselves as leader. Only the current leader is allowed
to pull waiting players out of the join queue and seat them in the shared
lobby, which has a fixed player capacity. Leadership uses failover: if the
leader crashes it drops back to a vacant state, and any node in the pool
may then be chosen in the next election to take over. While the lobby is
leaderless, ordinary players cannot be admitted -- their join requests just
accumulate in the bounded queue. The twist is a privileged admin override:
an operator can force-admit a queued player straight into the lobby even
while no leader is present, skipping the leader gate entirely for
emergencies such as a stalled failover. That override is still bound by the
same lobby capacity as an ordinary admission -- it can bypass the leader
requirement but never the seat limit -- and each override use is tallied in
a saturating audit counter. Players already seated can also leave the lobby
at any time, freeing a seat. The full action set is: RequestJoin (a player
joins the bounded wait queue if it has room), ElectLeader (when no leader
is present, one of the matchmaker nodes is chosen as the new leader),
LeaderFail (the current leader crashes and the lobby becomes leaderless),
LeaderAdmit (the leader dequeues one waiting player and seats them if the
lobby is under capacity), AdminOverrideAdmit (the admin force-admits one
waiting player into the lobby if it is under capacity, regardless of
whether a leader is present, and increments the saturating override
counter), and PlayerLeave (a seated player departs, freeing one seat).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of players seated in the lobby never goes
negative and never exceeds the fixed capacity, whether a seat was granted
by the elected leader or forced by the privileged admin override.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: whenever the lobby becomes leaderless after a failure,
a new leader is eventually elected, so failover never leaves the
matchmaker permanently without a leader.

---- MODULE W4Od18m3p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Device, Slot, NoLeader, NoOwner, MaxTerm, MaxVersion

ASSUME NoLeader \notin Device
ASSUME NoOwner \notin Device

VARIABLES leader, term, slotVersion, allocations

vars == <<leader, term, slotVersion, allocations>>

\* Every grant (leader, admin, or release) is stamped with the slot's version
\* counter and bumps it; only the entry matching a slot's CURRENT counter is
\* live, so stale entries from before a failover or override are automatically
\* superseded rather than needing to be deleted.

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Device \cup {NoLeader}
  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ slotVersion \in [Slot -> 0..MaxVersion]
  /\ allocations \subseteq [slot: Slot, dev: Device \cup {NoOwner}, version: 0..MaxVersion]

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ term = 0
  /\ slotVersion = [s \in Slot |-> 0]
  /\ allocations = {[slot |-> s, dev |-> NoOwner, version |-> 0] : s \in Slot}

\* True when device d holds the current, live grant entry for slot s.
Assigned(s, d) ==
  \E r \in allocations : r.slot = s /\ r.dev = d /\ r.version = slotVersion[s]

Elect ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ \E d \in Device :
       /\ d # leader
       /\ leader' = d
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotVersion, allocations>>

LeaderGrant(d, s) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ Assigned(s, NoOwner)
  /\ slotVersion[s] < MaxVersion
  /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ allocations' = allocations \cup {[slot |-> s, dev |-> d, version |-> slotVersion'[s]]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

AdminOverride(d, s) ==
  /\ slotVersion[s] < MaxVersion
  /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ allocations' = allocations \cup {[slot |-> s, dev |-> d, version |-> slotVersion'[s]]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

ReleaseSlot(s) ==
  /\ ~ Assigned(s, NoOwner)
  /\ slotVersion[s] < MaxVersion
  /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ allocations' = allocations \cup {[slot |-> s, dev |-> NoOwner, version |-> slotVersion'[s]]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

Next ==
  \/ Elect
  \/ \E d \in Device, s \in Slot : LeaderGrant(d, s)
  \/ \E d \in Device, s \in Slot : AdminOverride(d, s)
  \/ \E s \in Slot : ReleaseSlot(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: whenever two grant entries are both live for a slot, they name the
\* same device -- an implication, not a raw count, so admin overrides that
\* correctly supersede the prior entry can never leave two devices holding
\* one slot at once.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
  \A s \in Slot, d1, d2 \in Device :
    (Assigned(s, d1) /\ Assigned(s, d2)) => d1 = d2

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
Device = {dev1, dev2, dev3}
Slot = {slotA, slotB}
NoLeader = NoLeader
NoOwner = NoOwner
MaxTerm = 3
MaxVersion = 3

INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A smart-home door lock network runs a small pool of controller devices that
coordinate which controller is allowed to grant door-access slots. At any
time at most one controller is the elected leader, and only the leader may
normally hand a slot to a requesting device. Leadership can fail over: a new
controller can be elected at any point, bumping the network's election term,
after which the previous leader loses its authority. Every grant of a slot
-- whether an initial hand-out, a release back to nobody, or a re-grant to a
different device -- is recorded as a new entry stamped with the slot's
current version counter, and the counter is incremented in the same step.
Only the entry whose stamped version matches the slot's live version counter
is the slot's current, binding assignment; earlier entries for that slot are
automatically superseded and carry no authority. The twist is that the
network also exposes a privileged admin override: an admin may reassign any
slot directly, without needing to be the elected leader, but the override
goes through the exact same version-stamped grant step as an ordinary
leader grant, so it also supersedes whatever entry was previously live for
that slot. The full action set is: electing a new leader (advancing the
term), the leader granting a slot to a device, the admin overriding a slot's
assignment directly, and releasing a slot back to no owner.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every slot, the set of live (version-current) grant
entries never names two different devices as holding that slot at once --
not even when the privileged admin override is the one doing the granting.

---- MODULE W4Od14m4p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS f1, f2, f3, MaxCapacity, MinCapacity

Alerts == {f1, f2, f3}

VARIABLES capacity, pending, queued, processing

vars == <<capacity, pending, queued, processing>>

\* Bounded work queue with runtime-adjustable capacity: Admit only succeeds
\* while queued+processing is under the capacity bound (backpressure), and
\* Grow/ShrinkCapacity retune that bound without touching admitted alerts.

Init ==
  /\ capacity = MinCapacity
  /\ pending = Alerts
  /\ queued = {}
  /\ processing = {}

GrowCapacity ==
  /\ capacity < MaxCapacity
  /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queued, processing>>

ShrinkCapacity ==
  /\ capacity > MinCapacity
  /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, queued, processing>>

Admit(a) ==
  /\ a \in pending
  /\ Cardinality(queued) + Cardinality(processing) < capacity
  /\ pending' = pending \ {a}
  /\ queued' = queued \cup {a}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, processing>>

StartProcessing(a) ==
  /\ a \in queued
  /\ queued' = queued \ {a}
  /\ processing' = processing \cup {a}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, pending>>

Complete(a) ==
  /\ a \in processing
  /\ processing' = processing \ {a}
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {a}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, queued>>

Next ==
  \/ GrowCapacity
  \/ ShrinkCapacity
  \/ \E a \in Alerts : Admit(a)
  \/ \E a \in Alerts : StartProcessing(a)
  \/ \E a \in Alerts : Complete(a)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(StartProcessing(f1) \/ Complete(f1))
  /\ WF_vars(StartProcessing(f2) \/ Complete(f2))
  /\ WF_vars(StartProcessing(f3) \/ Complete(f3))

\* Conservation: every alert sits in exactly one bucket, so none is ever
\* created, duplicated, or dropped, however the capacity bound is retuned.
AlertConservation ==
  /\ pending \cup queued \cup processing = Alerts
  /\ pending \cap queued = {}
  /\ pending \cap processing = {}
  /\ queued \cap processing = {}

\* Every alert admitted into the queue or picked up for processing
\* eventually cycles back out to pending -- no alert is ever stranded.
AlertsDrain ==
  \A a \in Alerts : (a \in queued \/ a \in processing) ~> (a \in pending)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  f1 = f1
  f2 = f2
  f3 = f3
  MaxCapacity = 3
  MinCapacity = 1

INVARIANT AlertConservation
PROPERTY AlertsDrain
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm patrols a fire-prone wilderness, and each
drone continuously re-scans its assigned area for new ignition alerts.
Because the ground command center can only staff a limited number of alerts
for active response at any moment, a newly detected alert must first queue
for triage before a response crew is dispatched to it: this is a bounded
work queue with backpressure -- an alert can only be admitted into the queue
if the number of alerts currently queued or already being actively
processed by response crews is below the queue's current capacity bound. That
capacity bound is not fixed: the command center grows it when it brings on
additional response crews (reinforcements arrive) and shrinks it when crews
are pulled off (redeployed to a larger blaze elsewhere), and this retuning
can happen at any time, independent of how many alerts are currently in
flight and without touching any alert already admitted. An alert that cannot
yet be admitted because the queue is at its capacity bound simply remains
pending, to be re-detected and retried on a later patrol pass. The full
action set is: GrowCapacity, where the command center raises the capacity
bound by one (up to a maximum); ShrinkCapacity, where the command center
lowers the capacity bound by one (down to a minimum), without touching any
alert already admitted into the queue or under processing; Admit, where a
pending alert is moved into the queue provided the current queued-plus-
processing count is still strictly below the capacity bound; StartProcessing,
where a queued alert is picked up by a response crew and moves to active
processing; and Complete, where an actively processed alert is resolved and
returned to pending, ready to be re-detected and re-admitted on a future
patrol pass.

SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, every alert is accounted for in
exactly one of pending, queued, or actively processing, so no alert is ever
created, duplicated, or silently dropped, regardless of how many times the
runtime capacity bound has grown or shrunk.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: every alert that is admitted into the queue or picked up
for active processing is eventually returned to pending, so no alert can be
admitted and then left stuck in the queue or with a response crew forever.

---- MODULE W4Od4m0p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, MaxVersion, MaxRetries

\* NoCar marks the wash bay as unoccupied.
NoCar == "NoCar"

VARIABLES state, version, localVer, holder, retries

vars == <<state, version, localVer, holder, retries>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ state \in [Cars -> {"idle", "reading", "washing"}]
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ localVer \in [Cars -> 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ holder \in Cars \cup {NoCar}
    /\ retries \in [Cars -> 0..MaxRetries]

Init ==
    /\ state = [c \in Cars |-> "idle"]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ localVer = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ holder = NoCar
    /\ retries = [c \in Cars |-> 0]

\* Optimistic-lock read: a waiting car snapshots the bay's live version
\* before deciding whether its claim would succeed.
Read(c) ==
    /\ state[c] = "idle"
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![c] = "reading"]
    /\ localVer' = [localVer EXCEPT ![c] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, holder, retries>>

\* CAS succeeds: the snapshot still matches the live version and the bay is
\* currently free, so the claim is granted and the version is bumped so
\* stale readers (including ones who read while occupied) see a conflict.
Enter(c) ==
    /\ state[c] = "reading"
    /\ localVer[c] = version
    /\ holder = NoCar
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![c] = "washing"]
    /\ holder' = c
    /\ version' = IF version = MaxVersion THEN 0 ELSE version + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<localVer, retries>>

\* CAS fails: another car's claim moved the version. The mechanism never
\* evicts a slow car -- it just re-snapshots and waits to retry again.
Retry(c) ==
    /\ state[c] = "reading"
    /\ localVer[c] # version
    /\ localVer' = [localVer EXCEPT ![c] = version]
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![c] =
                     IF retries[c] < MaxRetries THEN retries[c] + 1 ELSE retries[c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, version, holder>>

Exit(c) ==
    /\ state[c] = "washing"
    /\ holder = c
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ holder' = NoCar
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, localVer, retries>>

Next == \E c \in Cars : Read(c) \/ Enter(c) \/ Retry(c) \/ Exit(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion of the wash bay stated as coherence between each car's
\* local state and the single recorded holder, rather than a bare count:
\* a car is washing if and only if it is the holder, so at most one can be.
MutualExclusion == \A c \in Cars : (state[c] = "washing") <=> (holder = c)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2, c3}
    MaxVersion = 3
    MaxRetries = 2
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line moves cars through a single wash bay, the critical
resource that only one car may occupy while being washed. Access to the wash
bay is coordinated by optimistic locking with retry: instead of taking a lock
up front, a waiting car first reads the wash bay's current version number as
a snapshot. It then attempts to claim the bay by comparing its saved snapshot
against the bay's live version and checking that the bay currently has no
holder. If the version still matches and the bay is free, the claim
succeeds: the car enters the wash bay, becomes the bay's recorded holder, and
the version number is bumped so that any other car holding a now-stale
snapshot -- including one who read while the bay was occupied -- will detect
the conflict on its own next attempt. If the version has moved on, the car
does not force its way in and is not removed from consideration; it simply
re-reads the live version and waits to try its claim again. A car in this waiting-to-retry state can be arbitrarily slow -- it may
re-read and retry as many times as it likes -- but the line has no
failure-detection or eviction mechanism, so a slow car is never treated as
failed or dropped from the queue, only left to retry patiently. Once a car
finishes washing it exits the bay and clears itself as holder, freeing the
bay for the next successful claim. The full action set is: a car reading the
bay's current version to take a snapshot, a car's claim succeeding because
its snapshot still matches the live version and the bay is free (entering the
bay, becoming its holder, and bumping the version), a car's claim failing
because the version has moved on (re-reading and retrying without being
evicted), and a car exiting the bay once it finishes washing.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the wash bay is never occupied by more than one car at a
time -- whenever a car is in the washing state it is exactly the bay's
recorded holder, and no other car can simultaneously hold that status.

spec_text:

\* Optimistic locking with retry: a participant snapshots the live version

\* snapshot still matches; a stale snapshot is repaired by Retry, never by

Init ==
  /\ state = [p \in Participants |-> "idle"]
  /\ commitHolder = NULL
  /\ version = 0
  /\ snapshot = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
  /\ crashed = FALSE

Request(p) ==
  /\ state[p] = "idle"
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![p] = "waiting"]
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![p] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<commitHolder, version, crashed>>

Retry(p) ==
  /\ state[p] = "waiting"
  /\ snapshot[p] # version
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![p] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<state, commitHolder, version, crashed>>

Acquire(p) ==
  /\ state[p] = "waiting"
  /\ commitHolder = NULL
  /\ snapshot[p] = version
  /\ commitHolder' = p
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![p] = "committing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, snapshot, crashed>>

Release(p) ==
  /\ state[p] = "committing"
  /\ commitHolder = p
  /\ commitHolder' = NULL
  /\ version' = (version + 1) % (MaxVersion + 1)
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![p] = "done"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snapshot, crashed>>

  /\ ~crashed
  /\ state[CrashP] = "committing"
  /\ commitHolder = CrashP
  /\ crashed' = TRUE
  /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![CrashP] = "crashed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<commitHolder, version, snapshot>>

Recover ==

  /\ commitHolder = CrashP
  /\ commitHolder' = NULL
  /\ UNCHANGED <<state, version, snapshot, crashed>>

RetryStep == \E p \in Participants : Retry(p)
AcquireStep == \E p \in Participants : Acquire(p)

nl:
A university course-registration system lets a fixed set of participants
(students) compete for the single critical resource that finalizes an
enrollment write: the shared "commit" slot on the registrar's record. The
system uses optimistic locking with retry: a participant who wants to
register first snapshots the record's current version number without
taking any lock (Request). If a participant's remembered snapshot no
longer matches the live version -- because someone else already
committed and bumped it -- the participant simply re-reads the version and
keeps waiting (Retry), instead of blocking. A participant may attempt to
acquire the critical resource only when its snapshot still matches the
live version and the resource is currently free (Acquire); this is the one
moment where exclusive access is required, because writing the enrollment
record must not interleave with another participant's write. Holding the
resource, the participant may finish normally, writing its enrollment and
bumping the version so the resource becomes free again (Release). The
twist: one designated participant can crash silently while it holds the
resource, after having acquired it but before releasing it (CrashWhileCommitting)
-- it simply stops taking steps and never calls Release. Because the
registration system cannot tell a crashed holder from a slow one, it runs a
recovery action that reclaims the resource from that specific crashed
participant once it has been marked crashed, freeing it for the remaining
participants (Recover). The full action set is: Request, Retry, Acquire,
Release, CrashWhileCommitting, and Recover.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The commit-slot pointer always stays coherent with each
participant's phase -- whoever the pointer names is either actively
committing or has crashed while holding it, and no participant other than
the one the pointer names is ever in the committing phase, so the critical
resource is never held by two participants at once even accounting for the
silent crash.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever the critical resource is held by some
participant, it is eventually released -- either the holder finishes
normally and releases it, or, if that holder is the one that crashed
silently, the recovery action eventually reclaims it -- so the resource
never stays stuck forever.

\* though queue order is not.

    /\ QueueSet \cap done = {}
    /\ QueueSet \cap waiting = {}
    /\ inOR \cap done = {}
    /\ inOR \cap waiting = {}
    /\ done \cap waiting = {}

    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ inOR = {}
    /\ done = {}

    /\ done' = done \cup {c}

in an admission pool before being placed into a bounded work queue that feeds
the hospital's operating rooms. The queue enforces backpressure: a case can
only be admitted into the queue while the queue has spare capacity, so
admission of new cases stalls once the queue is full. Once queued, a case is
dequeued into an operating room whenever an OR is free, and once surgery
finishes the case is marked completed. Case-request messages travel over an

the relative order of cases still sitting in the queue, meaning the case
dequeued next does not have to be the one that was admitted first. The full
action set is: Admit (moves a case from the waiting pool into the queue,
blocked by backpressure when the queue is at capacity), Reorder (swaps the
positions of two cases currently in the queue, modeling in-transit message
reordering), Dequeue (moves the case at the front of the queue into a free
operating room), and Complete (moves a case out of its operating room into
the completed set once surgery is done). Throughout all of this shuffling,
scheduling, and completion, no case is ever created, duplicated, or dropped:
every case must remain in exactly one of the waiting pool, the queue, an
operating room, or the completed set. SAFETY PROPERTY: every surgical case is
accounted for in exactly one of the waiting pool, the queue, an operating
room, or the completed set at all times, with no case appearing in more than
one of these places and no case missing from all of them, even after the
queue is reordered.

\* hold so a stale, reordered grant from an earlier epoch can never be honored.

  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ holding' = [c \in Controllers |-> FALSE]
  /\ holdEpoch' = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]

\* stamped with the current epoch; the network may reorder/delay it.
IssueGrant ==
  /\ \A c \in Controllers : ~holding[c]
  /\ \E c \in Controllers :
       /\ [ctrl |-> c, ep |-> epoch] \notin pending
       /\ pending' = pending \cup {[ctrl |-> c, ep |-> epoch]}

\* grant issued for a since-superseded epoch is discarded as stale instead
\* of being honored -- this is what preserves mutual exclusion under reordering.

       /\ pending' = pending \ {m}
       /\ IF m.ep = epoch /\ (\A c \in Controllers : ~holding[c])

                 /\ holdEpoch' = [holdEpoch EXCEPT ![m.ctrl] = m.ep]
            ELSE /\ holding' = holding
                 /\ holdEpoch' = holdEpoch

the queue and grants it any slot that is not currently occupied. Separately,

slot to an arbitrary car at any time, jumping the queue entirely and ignoring

currently occupies its target slot as part of the same step before granting
it to the new car. A car that has finished washing may leave its slot at any
time, freeing that slot for the next grant. The full action set is: a car
arriving into the bounded queue, ordinary dispatch of the queue's head car
into a free slot, the admin override granting a slot directly (evicting any
current occupant first), and a washed car departing its slot.

and backpressure, no wash slot is ever recorded as allocated to two different
cars at the same time -- the literal no-double-allocation-of-the-same-slot
property.

NoReq == [amt |-> 0, votes |-> 0]

TypeInv == /\ pool \in 0..InitPool
           /\ reserve1 \in 0..InitPool
           /\ reserve2 \in 0..InitPool
           /\ req1.amt \in 0..MaxAmt /\ req1.votes \in 0..N
           /\ req2.amt \in 0..MaxAmt /\ req2.votes \in 0..N

Init == /\ pool = InitPool
        /\ reserve1 = 0
        /\ reserve2 = 0
        /\ req1 = NoReq
        /\ req2 = NoReq

\* Propose earmarks (removes) the amount from the shared pool immediately,
\* so a later commit can never be starved by the other instance draining
\* the pool out from under an already-voted proposal.
Propose1(amt) == /\ req1.amt = 0
                 /\ amt \in 1..MaxAmt
                 /\ amt <= pool
                 /\ pool' = pool - amt
                 /\ req1' = [amt |-> amt, votes |-> 1]
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<reserve1, reserve2, req2>>

Vote1 == /\ req1.amt > 0
         /\ req1.votes < N
         /\ req1' = [req1 EXCEPT !.votes = @ + 1]
         /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserve1, reserve2, req2>>

Commit1 == /\ req1.amt > 0
           /\ req1.votes >= Quorum
           /\ reserve1' = reserve1 + req1.amt
           /\ req1' = NoReq
           /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserve2, req2>>

Propose2(amt) == /\ req2.amt = 0
                 /\ amt \in 1..MaxAmt
                 /\ amt <= pool
                 /\ pool' = pool - amt
                 /\ req2' = [amt |-> amt, votes |-> 1]
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<reserve1, reserve2, req1>>

Vote2 == /\ req2.amt > 0
         /\ req2.votes < N
         /\ req2' = [req2 EXCEPT !.votes = @ + 1]
         /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserve1, reserve2, req1>>

Commit2 == /\ req2.amt > 0
           /\ req2.votes >= Quorum
           /\ reserve2' = reserve2 + req2.amt
           /\ req2' = NoReq
           /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, reserve1, req1>>

Next == \/ \E amt \in 1..MaxAmt : Propose1(amt)
        \/ Vote1
        \/ Commit1
        \/ \E amt \in 1..MaxAmt : Propose2(amt)
        \/ Vote2
        \/ Commit2

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Vote1) /\ WF_vars(Commit1)
             /\ WF_vars(Vote2) /\ WF_vars(Commit2)

\* Conservation: funds are always in exactly one of the shared pool, an
\* instance's earmarked-but-uncommitted proposal, or a settled reserve;
\* the four-way sum never drifts from the pool's initial funding, so
\* nothing is created or destroyed.
Conservation == pool + reserve1 + reserve2 + req1.amt + req2.amt = InitPool

\* Progress: an outstanding proposal cannot stall forever waiting on votes.
LivenessProperty == /\ (req1.amt > 0 ~> req1.amt = 0)
                     /\ (req2.amt > 0 ~> req2.amt = 0)

=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    N = 3
    Quorum = 2
    InitPool = 4
    MaxAmt = 2

INVARIANT Conservation

PROPERTY LivenessProperty

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In a bank's interbank settlement batch, two independent settlement instances
(instance 1 and instance 2) periodically withdraw approved amounts from a
single reserve pool that both instances share. To move funds out of the
shared pool, each instance's operator proposes a withdrawal amount; the
amount is immediately earmarked out of the shared pool at proposal time (so
one instance can never be starved by the other later draining the pool out
from under an already-earmarked proposal), and participating banks cast
votes on the proposal (the proposer's own vote counts as the first one).
The withdrawal only commits once at least Quorum of the N possible votes
have been cast. Instance 1 supports Propose1 (earmark a new withdrawal
amount out of the shared pool when none is pending), Vote1 (cast an
additional vote on instance 1's pending withdrawal), and Commit1 (move the
already-earmarked amount into instance 1's settled reserve once quorum is
reached); instance 2 supports the symmetric Propose2, Vote2, and Commit2
actions. Because the two instances draw from the same shared pool, an
earmark made by one instance reduces what remains available for the other
to propose. SAFETY PROPERTY: at every point, the shared pool balance plus
both instances' earmarked-but-uncommitted amounts plus both instances'
settled reserves equals the pool's initial funding, so no funds are ever
created or destroyed as they move between the shared pool, an in-flight
proposal, and either instance's reserve. LIVENESS PROPERTY: whenever either
instance has a pending withdrawal proposal outstanding, that proposal is
eventually committed (cleared) rather than stalling forever waiting on
votes.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m7p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, NumBlocks, Capacity, VersionBound

ASSUME NumBlocks \in Nat \ {0}
ASSUME Capacity \in Nat \ {0}
ASSUME VersionBound \in Nat \ {0}

Blocks == 1..NumBlocks

VARIABLES trainLoc, occ, version, crashed

vars == <<trainLoc, occ, version, crashed>>

(* occ/version is a compare-and-swap register pair per signalling block:
   an action first compares occ[b] against Capacity, then swaps both
   fields together. The version tag has fixed width (wraps mod
   VersionBound), matching a real bounded ABA counter. trainLoc[t] = 0
   means train t is idle in the yard. *)

Init ==
  /\ trainLoc = [t \in Trains |-> 0]
  /\ occ = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ version = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ crashed = {}

CasEnter(t) ==
  LET b == 1 IN
  /\ t \notin crashed
  /\ trainLoc[t] = 0
  /\ occ[b] < Capacity
  /\ trainLoc' = [trainLoc EXCEPT ![t] = b]
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = (@ + 1) % VersionBound]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

Advance(t, b) ==
  /\ t \notin crashed
  /\ trainLoc[t] = b
  /\ b < NumBlocks
  /\ occ[b + 1] < Capacity
  /\ trainLoc' = [trainLoc EXCEPT ![t] = b + 1]
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1, ![b + 1] = @ + 1]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = (@ + 1) % VersionBound,
                                 ![b + 1] = (@ + 1) % VersionBound]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

ExitTrack(t, b) ==
  /\ t \notin crashed
  /\ trainLoc[t] = b
  /\ b = NumBlocks
  /\ trainLoc' = [trainLoc EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
  /\ occ' = [occ EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
  /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = (@ + 1) % VersionBound]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

CrashSilently(t) ==
  (* The twist: a train can die inside a block without ever releasing the
     CAS register, permanently pinning that unit of occupancy forever. *)
  /\ t \notin crashed
  /\ trainLoc[t] # 0
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<trainLoc, occ, version>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains : CasEnter(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Advance(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : ExitTrack(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : CrashSilently(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityRespected ==
  (* Literal safety property: no block's CAS register ever records more
     trains than its declared capacity, whether or not a crash occurred. *)
  \A b \in Blocks : occ[b] <= Capacity

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Trains = {1, 2, 3}
    NumBlocks = 3
    Capacity = 2
    VersionBound = 4

INVARIANT CapacityRespected

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway signalling block system divides a stretch of track into a fixed
sequence of numbered blocks. Each block guards its own occupancy count with
a compare-and-swap register: before a train may enter a block, or advance
from one block into the next, the controller compares the block's current
occupancy against the block's fixed capacity and only then swaps the
register to the incremented value together with a version counter, so
concurrent entry attempts never both succeed against a stale reading. A
train starts idle in the yard, enters the first block when that block's
register admits it, advances block by block along the line, and finally
exits back to the yard once it clears the last block, decrementing the
register it leaves behind. The twist is that a train can crash silently
while it is sitting inside a block: it simply stops taking any further
action (it can never advance or exit again) without ever running the
release swap on that block's register, so the unit of capacity it was
holding stays permanently pinned even though the train is gone. The full
action set is: CasEnter (a yard-idle train enters block 1 if its register
has spare capacity), Advance (a train in block b moves into block b+1 if
that block's register has spare capacity), ExitTrack (a train in the last
block leaves to the yard, freeing its block's register), and CrashSilently
(a non-crashed train currently in some block is marked crashed, leaving all
registers untouched forever after). SAFETY PROPERTY: no signalling block's
compare-and-swap register ever records more trains occupying it than the
block's declared capacity, whether or not a train has silently crashed
inside it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m6p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Requesters, NoHolder

ASSUME NoHolder \notin Requesters

VARIABLES holder, epoch, pending, inFlight, inCS, submitted

vars == <<holder, epoch, pending, inFlight, inCS, submitted>>

\* Set of hospitals currently waiting in the FIFO reservation queue.
RangeSeq(s) == {s[i] : i \in 1..Len(s)}

Init ==
    /\ holder = NoHolder
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ pending = <<>>
    /\ inFlight = {}
    /\ inCS = {}
    /\ submitted = {}

\* A hospital submits its one-time reservation request for the unit.
Submit(r) ==
    /\ r \notin submitted
    /\ submitted' = submitted \cup {r}
    /\ pending' = Append(pending, r)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, inFlight, inCS>>

\* Manager grants the lease to the head of the queue and stamps the grant
\* confirmation with a fresh epoch (fencing token) so later/duplicate
\* confirmations from earlier holders can be told apart from this one.
GrantLease ==
    /\ holder = NoHolder
    /\ pending # <<>>
    /\ LET r == Head(pending)
           newEpoch == epoch + 1
       IN /\ holder' = r
          /\ epoch' = newEpoch
          /\ pending' = Tail(pending)
          /\ inFlight' = inFlight \cup {[dest |-> r, ep |-> newEpoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, submitted>>

\* Network delivery is unordered: any in-flight confirmation may arrive at
\* any time (this is where message reordering bites). A confirmation only
\* grants local custody if its epoch still matches the current lease;
\* otherwise it is a harmless stale duplicate and is simply dropped.
DeliverGrant ==
    /\ \E m \in inFlight :
        /\ inFlight' = inFlight \ {m}
        /\ inCS' = IF m.ep = epoch THEN inCS \cup {m.dest} ELSE inCS
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, pending, submitted>>

\* Holder voluntarily gives back the unit once its procedure is done.
Release ==
    /\ holder # NoHolder
    /\ inCS' = inCS \ {holder}
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ holder' = NoHolder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, inFlight, submitted>>

\* Lease expiry: the manager reclaims the unit from an unresponsive
\* holder even if that holder's own grant confirmation is still in
\* flight; the fencing token still advances, invalidating it in transit.
ExpireLease ==
    /\ holder # NoHolder
    /\ inCS' = inCS \ {holder}
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ holder' = NoHolder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, inFlight, submitted>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Requesters : Submit(r)
    \/ GrantLease
    \/ DeliverGrant
    \/ Release
    \/ ExpireLease

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(GrantLease) /\ WF_vars(DeliverGrant) /\ WF_vars(ExpireLease)

\* Mutual exclusion is the literal safety property for this cell: at most
\* one hospital may simultaneously hold a delivered, still-current grant
\* confirmation for the single critical blood unit.
MutualExclusion == Cardinality(inCS) <= 1

\* Every hospital that ever queues a request is eventually granted the
\* lease, regardless of confirmation reordering or intervening expiries.
EventualGrant == \A r \in Requesters : (r \in RangeSeq(pending)) ~> (holder = r)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Requesters = {h1, h2, h3}
    NoHolder = NoHolder
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY EventualGrant
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker coordinates hospitals that need exclusive, temporary custody of a single scarce blood unit reserved for an urgent transfusion. Hospitals submit a one-time request to reserve the unit; the tracker's lease manager queues these requests in the order they arrive and, whenever the unit is free, grants a time-limited lease to the hospital at the front of the queue. Each grant is stamped with a fresh lease epoch (a fencing token), and the grant confirmation is sent to the hospital over a network that can reorder, delay, or duplicate messages, so a confirmation may arrive long after it was issued -- including after the lease it refers to has already ended. A hospital's local view of holding the unit only becomes official once its grant confirmation is delivered and its epoch still matches the tracker's current lease; confirmations whose epoch the tracker has already moved past are recognized as stale and discarded rather than honored. A lease ends either because the holding hospital voluntarily releases the unit once its procedure is complete, or because the tracker unilaterally reclaims it after the lease's expiry timer runs out, even if that hospital's own grant confirmation has not yet been delivered; either way, ending a lease advances the fencing token so that any confirmation still in flight for the ended lease can no longer be mistaken for a valid current grant. The full action set is: a hospital submitting its one-time reservation request, the tracker granting the lease to the hospital at the head of the queue, the network delivering a (possibly stale) grant confirmation, the holding hospital voluntarily releasing the unit, and the tracker expiring an unresponsive hospital's lease.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one hospital ever regards itself, via a delivered and still-current grant confirmation, as holding the critical blood unit at the same time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every hospital that submits a reservation request is eventually granted the lease on the blood unit, regardless of how the network reorders or delays grant confirmations or how many leases expire before it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m3p5t3 ----
\* Wildfire drone swarm: leader election with failover, fenced by a term
\* counter, guards a single irreversible backburn-ignition action. A drone
\* can be "slow" but is never removed from the swarm, so a stale proposal
\* from a superseded (merely slow, not dead) leader can still be sitting
\* in the network after failover moves the term forward past it.
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Drones, MaxTerm

VARIABLES term, leader, status, pending, ignitionLog

vars == <<term, leader, status, pending, ignitionLog>>

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = "none"
    /\ status = [d \in Drones |-> "active"]
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ ignitionLog = <<>>

Elect(d) ==
    /\ leader = "none"
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, pending, ignitionLog>>

Failover(d) ==
    /\ leader # "none"
    /\ d # leader
    /\ status[d] = "active"
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, pending, ignitionLog>>

ToggleStatus(d) ==
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![d] = IF status[d] = "active" THEN "slow" ELSE "active"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, pending, ignitionLog>>

Propose ==
    /\ leader # "none"
    /\ Len(ignitionLog) = 0
    /\ [drone |-> leader, t |-> term] \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[drone |-> leader, t |-> term]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, status, ignitionLog>>

Commit(p) ==
    /\ p \in pending
    /\ p.t = term
    /\ ignitionLog' = Append(ignitionLog, p)
    /\ pending' = pending \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, status>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Elect(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Failover(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : ToggleStatus(d)
    \/ Propose
    \/ \E p \in pending : Commit(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

IgnitionAtMostOnce ==
    /\ Len(ignitionLog) <= 1
    /\ (Len(ignitionLog) = 1 => ignitionLog[1].t <= term)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {d1, d2, d3}
    MaxTerm = 4
INVARIANT IgnitionAtMostOnce
nl:
In a wildfire drone surveillance swarm, drones patrol a fire perimeter and
elect a leader to coordinate response. The swarm uses leader election with
failover: if the current leader appears unresponsive, another active drone
can take over leadership, and each election or failover bumps a fencing
term so that stale messages from a superseded leader cannot be mistaken for
current ones. Only the current leader may propose the swarm's single
irreversible action -- igniting a controlled backburn to starve the
wildfire of fuel -- and once a proposal commits, the backburn is lit and
cannot be undone. Drones in this swarm can be slow to respond because of
weak radio links or heavy onboard computation, but a slow drone is never
presumed failed or removed from the swarm: it remains a full member,
eligible to later resume normal responsiveness, and any ignition proposal
it made while it was still leader may still be sitting unresolved in the
network when failover later hands leadership to someone else. The swarm has
five actions: electing an initial leader when none is set, failing over
leadership to a new active drone while bumping the term, toggling a single
drone between active and slow responsiveness (drones are never marked
failed or removed), the current leader proposing a backburn ignition
tagged with the term under which it leads, and committing a pending
proposal whose tag still matches the current term. SAFETY PROPERTY: the
backburn ignition commits at most once overall, even when a slow (not
failed) former leader's stale ignition proposal is still pending in the
network after failover has already advanced the term past it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m6p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Workers, Jobs, NoWorker, LeaseDuration, MaxClock, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES clock, holder, epoch, expiry, printed, heldEpoch

vars == <<clock, holder, epoch, expiry, printed, heldEpoch>>

\* Mechanism: each job's lease carries a fencing epoch bumped on every
\* hand-off. A worker only remembers the epoch it captured when it took
\* the lease. Print (the irreversible action) commits only if that
\* remembered epoch still matches the job's live epoch, so a slow
\* worker whose lease has since been reassigned gets fenced off instead
\* of double-printing a job someone faster already finished.

TypeOK ==
    /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
    /\ holder \in [Jobs -> Workers \cup {NoWorker}]
    /\ epoch \in [Jobs -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ expiry \in [Jobs -> 0..(MaxClock + LeaseDuration)]
    /\ printed \in [Jobs -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ heldEpoch \in [Workers -> [Jobs -> 0..MaxEpoch]]

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ holder = [j \in Jobs |-> NoWorker]
    /\ epoch = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]
    /\ expiry = [j \in Jobs |-> 0]
    /\ printed = [j \in Jobs |-> FALSE]
    /\ heldEpoch = [w \in Workers |-> [j \in Jobs |-> 0]]

\* Take an unheld or expired job, bump its epoch, and remember that epoch.
AcquireLease(w, j) ==
    /\ ~printed[j]
    /\ epoch[j] < MaxEpoch
    /\ \/ holder[j] = NoWorker
       \/ clock >= expiry[j]
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![j] = w]
    /\ epoch' = [epoch EXCEPT ![j] = epoch[j] + 1]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![j] = clock + LeaseDuration]
    /\ heldEpoch' = [heldEpoch EXCEPT ![w] = [@ EXCEPT ![j] = epoch[j] + 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, printed>>

ReleaseLease(w, j) ==
    /\ holder[j] = w
    /\ ~printed[j]
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![j] = NoWorker]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, epoch, expiry, printed, heldEpoch>>

\* The irreversible commit: fenced by the worker's remembered epoch.
Print(w, j) ==
    /\ ~printed[j]
    /\ heldEpoch[w][j] > 0
    /\ heldEpoch[w][j] = epoch[j]
    /\ printed' = [printed EXCEPT ![j] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, epoch, expiry, heldEpoch>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, expiry, printed, heldEpoch>>

\* Once every job is printed the spooler has nothing left to do; it idles
\* rather than deadlocking the state graph.
Quiescent ==
    /\ \A j \in Jobs : printed[j]
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

AnyAcquire == \E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : AcquireLease(w, j)
AnyRelease == \E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : ReleaseLease(w, j)
AnyPrint == \E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs : Print(w, j)

Next == AnyAcquire \/ AnyRelease \/ AnyPrint \/ Tick \/ Quiescent

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(AnyAcquire) /\ WF_vars(AnyPrint)
             /\ WF_vars(AnyRelease) /\ WF_vars(Tick)

\* Safety: a printed job is always traceable to a worker whose recorded
\* epoch had not yet been superseded -- no stale lease-holder's print
\* attempt is ever the one that actually committed.
PrintAuthorized ==
    \A j \in Jobs :
        printed[j] =>
            \E w \in Workers : heldEpoch[w][j] = epoch[j] /\ heldEpoch[w][j] > 0

\* Liveness: no job is stuck forever behind a fenced-off straggler.
EventuallyAllPrinted == \A j \in Jobs : <> printed[j]

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    Jobs = {j1, j2}
    NoWorker = NoWorker
    LeaseDuration = 2
    MaxClock = 5
    MaxEpoch = 3

INVARIANT PrintAuthorized
PROPERTY EventuallyAllPrinted
nl:
A print shop spooler hands incoming jobs to a small pool of operators. To
work a job an operator must acquire a time-bounded lease naming it the
current owner; the lease carries a fencing epoch that is bumped every time
the job changes hands. An operator may voluntarily release a job's lease,
and once a lease's expiry time has passed any operator may re-acquire the
job -- even though the operator who held it has not crashed. It may simply
be running behind on that job (slow, not failed), still intending to finish
it later. Printing a job is the irreversible action: once paper comes out of
the machine it cannot be recalled. An operator's print attempt only commits
if the fencing epoch it captured when it took the lease still equals the
job's current epoch; if a slow operator's lease has since been reassigned to
someone else, the epoch check fails and the straggler's late print attempt
is rejected, so a job already printed by a faster operator can never be
printed again by the operator that fell behind. The full action set is:
AcquireLease (an operator takes an unheld or expired, not-yet-printed job at
the current clock, bumps its epoch, and records that new epoch for itself),
ReleaseLease (the current holder voluntarily gives up an unprinted job),
Print (an operator whose recorded epoch for a job still equals the job's
live epoch commits the irreversible print), Tick (the shop's clock
advances, which is what lets a lease's expiry actually pass), and
Quiescent (once every job in the shop has been printed, the spooler simply
idles). SAFETY
PROPERTY: each job is printed at most once, because every completed print is
attributable to an operator whose recorded lease epoch had not yet been
superseded at the moment it fired, even when the operator that eventually
prints it was merely slow rather than failed. LIVENESS PROPERTY: every job
is eventually printed, since a slow operator's stale attempt being fenced
off never stalls the job forever -- the lease keeps moving until some
operator with a live epoch actually prints it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m0p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Participants, CrashParticipant, MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, authorized, crashed, partVersion, orders, authVersion

vars == <<version, authorized, crashed, partVersion, orders, authVersion>>

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ authorized = Participants
  /\ crashed = {}
  /\ partVersion = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
  /\ authVersion = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
  /\ orders = {}

\* Sync is the read half of optimistic locking: a participant refreshes its
\* cached version so a later SubmitOrder's compare-and-swap can succeed.
Sync(p) ==
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ partVersion[p] < version
  /\ partVersion' = [partVersion EXCEPT ![p] = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, authorized, crashed, orders, authVersion>>

\* SubmitOrder is the CAS-style commit: it only succeeds while the cached
\* version still matches the book's current version, else the caller is
\* stale and must Sync and retry.
SubmitOrder(p) ==
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ partVersion[p] = version
  /\ orders' = orders \cup {[part |-> p, ver |-> version]}
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ partVersion' = [partVersion EXCEPT ![p] = version']
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authorized, crashed, authVersion>>

\* RevokeAuth deauthorizes a participant and stamps the book version at
\* which authorization ended, so past orders can be checked against it.
RevokeAuth(p) ==
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ authorized' = authorized \ {p}
  /\ authVersion' = [authVersion EXCEPT ![p] = version]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, partVersion, orders>>

\* Crash is the twist: exactly one designated participant may silently drop
\* out, handled identically to RevokeAuth for staleness bookkeeping.
Crash(p) ==
  /\ p = CrashParticipant
  /\ p \in authorized
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
  /\ authorized' = authorized \ {p}
  /\ authVersion' = [authVersion EXCEPT ![p] = version]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<partVersion, orders>>

Next ==
  \E p \in Participants :
    \/ Sync(p)
    \/ SubmitOrder(p)
    \/ RevokeAuth(p)
    \/ Crash(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

StateConstraint == version <= MaxVersion

\* NoStaleAction: an order in the log either still belongs to a currently
\* authorized participant, or -- if that participant was later deauthorized
\* or crashed -- the order predates that event, so no unauthorized, revoked,
\* or silently-crashed participant's action is ever recorded as legitimate.
NoStaleAction ==
  \A o \in orders : \/ o.part \in authorized
                     \/ o.ver < authVersion[o.part]

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Participants = {1, 2, 3}
  CrashParticipant = 1
  MaxVersion = 4

INVARIANT NoStaleAction

CONSTRAINT StateConstraint

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction in which several participants
(brokers) submit orders during the pre-open phase before the market opens.
Access to the shared auction book is coordinated through optimistic locking
with retry: each participant caches a version number for the book, and to
commit an order it must present a cached version that still matches the
book's current version. If the version has since moved on -- because
another participant committed an order first, or because the exchange
revoked someone's access -- the stale participant's submission is rejected
and it must resynchronize by re-reading the current version before it can

designated participant may crash silently at any point: from that moment on

notification event that other participants could observe. The model's full
action set is: Sync (a participant refreshes its cached version to the

its cached version as an optimistic-locking token, which only succeeds if
that token still matches the book's current version, and which advances the
book's version on success), RevokeAuth (the exchange deauthorizes a
participant, recording the book version at which the deauthorization took
effect), and Crash (the one designated participant silently drops out,

belongs to a currently authorized participant, or -- if that participant
was later deauthorized or crashed -- the order was made strictly before
that deauthorization/crash event, so that no unauthorized, revoked, or
silently-crashed participant's action is ever recorded as legitimate.

record of that slot's owner, so no two requests can simultaneously and
legitimately hold the same slot. LIVENESS PROPERTY: every request whose
proposal is pending eventually has it resolved, either by winning the slot
through quorum commit or by cancelling after the admin reassigns the target
slot away.

\* slotOwner is the network's authoritative record; owns is each participant's
\* own belief. Optimistic commits only succeed if the read version still
\* matches, so a crashed participant's stale pending claim can never commit.

  /\ slotVersion = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ pendingSlot = [p \in Participants |-> NoSlot]
  /\ pendingVersion = [p \in Participants |-> 0]
  /\ owns = [p \in Participants |-> NoSlot]
  /\ crashed = {}

Read(p, s) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ pendingSlot[p] = NoSlot
  /\ owns[p] = NoSlot
  /\ slotOwner[s] = NoOwner
  /\ pendingSlot' = [pendingSlot EXCEPT ![p] = s]
  /\ pendingVersion' = [pendingVersion EXCEPT ![p] = slotVersion[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, owns, crashed>>

\* Commit is the compare-and-swap: it only succeeds if the slot is still free
\* and its version has not moved since the read, so a stale claim never wins.
Commit(p) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ pendingSlot[p] # NoSlot
  /\ LET s == pendingSlot[p] IN
       /\ slotOwner[s] = NoOwner
       /\ slotVersion[s] = pendingVersion[p]
       /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = p]
       /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
       /\ owns' = [owns EXCEPT ![p] = s]
  /\ pendingSlot' = [pendingSlot EXCEPT ![p] = NoSlot]
  /\ pendingVersion' = [pendingVersion EXCEPT ![p] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED crashed

RetryAbort(p) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ pendingSlot[p] # NoSlot
  /\ slotVersion[pendingSlot[p]] # pendingVersion[p]
  /\ pendingSlot' = [pendingSlot EXCEPT ![p] = NoSlot]
  /\ pendingVersion' = [pendingVersion EXCEPT ![p] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, owns, crashed>>

Release(p) ==
  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ owns[p] # NoSlot
  /\ LET s == owns[p] IN
       /\ slotOwner' = [slotOwner EXCEPT ![s] = NoOwner]
       /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ owns' = [owns EXCEPT ![p] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingSlot, pendingVersion, crashed>>

\* A silent crash freezes a participant forever: no more Read/Commit/Release,
\* and whatever it was holding (owned slot or pending claim) is never cleaned up.

  /\ p \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotOwner, slotVersion, pendingSlot, pendingVersion, owns>>

  \/ \E p \in Participants : Commit(p)
  \/ \E p \in Participants : RetryAbort(p)
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Release(p)

A smart-home door lock network manages a small set of access slots (physical
lock reservations, e.g. a delivery window or a guest-code period) that
household participants can claim. A participant claims a slot using optimistic
locking with retry: it first reads the slot's current version number, then
attempts to commit its claim only if the slot is still unowned and its
version has not changed since the read. If another participant already
committed a claim in between (the version moved), the read is stale and the
participant aborts the attempt and retries later rather than overwriting the
existing claim. Once a participant holds a slot it may release it, which
clears the owner and bumps the version so old reads can never be replayed as
valid. The twist: any one participant's hub controller can crash silently at
any point -- it simply stops taking further actions, possibly while holding a
pending read or a committed slot, and never cleans up after itself. The
network keeps two views of ownership: each participant's own belief about
which slot it holds, and the network's authoritative per-slot owner record.
The action set is: Read (a participant with no pending attempt inspects an
unowned slot's version and stakes a pending claim on it), Commit (a
participant with a pending claim finalizes it, becoming the slot's owner and
bumping the version, but only if the slot is still unowned and the version
still matches what it read), RetryAbort (a participant with a pending claim
whose version has gone stale drops the claim so it can try again later),
Release (a participant that owns a slot gives it up, clearing the owner and
bumping the version), and Crash (a participant's controller silently stops
acting, without releasing any slot it holds or clearing any pending claim).

agrees with the network's authoritative owner record for that slot, so no
slot is ever simultaneously believed owned by two different participants,
even when another participant's controller has crashed silently mid-claim.

  /\ localEpoch[m] = epoch
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = m]
  /\ ownerEpoch' = [ownerEpoch EXCEPT ![s] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, localEpoch, dispensed>>

\* A slow machine may still dispense from a slot it legitimately owns even
\* if later reconfigurations happened it hasn't synced to -- it is slow,
\* not failed, so its outstanding claim stays honored.
Dispense(m, s) ==
  /\ owner[s] = m
  /\ dispensed[s] = NoOwner
  /\ dispensed' = [dispensed EXCEPT ![s] = m]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owner, localEpoch, ownerEpoch>>

Release(m, s) ==
  /\ owner[s] = m
  /\ dispensed[s] = m
  /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = NoOwner]
  /\ dispensed' = [dispensed EXCEPT ![s] = NoOwner]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, localEpoch, ownerEpoch>>

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E m \in Machines : SyncEpoch(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines, s \in Slots : Allocate(m, s)
  \/ \E m \in Machines, s \in Slots : Dispense(m, s)
  \/ \E m \in Machines, s \in Slots : Release(m, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: whenever a slot has been dispensed to some machine,
\* that machine must still be the slot's recorded owner -- a second machine
\* can never simultaneously hold a live claim on the same slot.
SafeAllocation ==
  \A s \in Slots : dispensed[s] # NoOwner => owner[s] = dispensed[s]

nl:
A vending machine network shares out product slots across a small set of
restocking machines. Access to slots is organized around epoch-numbered
reconfiguration: an operator can bump a global epoch counter to mark the
start of a new configuration round, but bumping the epoch never seizes a
machine's existing slot claim -- a machine that has fallen behind on epoch
gossip is treated as slow, not failed, so its outstanding claims stay valid
and are never reassigned out from under it. To claim a free slot, a machine
must first have synced its own local epoch counter up to the current global
epoch; once it holds the claim, it may dispense the slot's product even if
further reconfigurations happen afterward that it hasn't heard about yet,
since a legitimately-held claim survives the machine's slowness. After
dispensing, the machine can release the slot, clearing it so another machine
may claim it in a later round. The full action set is: Reconfigure (bump the
global epoch, leaving all existing claims and dispenses untouched), SyncEpoch
(a machine catches its local epoch counter up to the current global epoch),
Allocate (a machine whose local epoch matches the current global epoch claims
a free, undispensed slot and stamps it with the current epoch), Dispense (the
current owner of a slot dispenses its product, recording itself as the
dispenser), and Release (a machine that both owns and has dispensed a slot
gives it up, clearing it for the next round). SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a
slot has been dispensed to some machine, that machine must still be the
slot's recorded owner, so a second machine can never simultaneously hold a
live claim on the same slot and double-allocate it -- even though a slow
machine's stale epoch view never gets forcibly evicted by reconfiguration.

---- MODULE W4Od7m4p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Slots, MinCap, MaxCap, MaxJobs

Jobs == 1..MaxJobs

VARIABLES capacity, queue, assignedList, free, nextJob, serviced

vars == <<capacity, queue, assignedList, free, nextJob, serviced>>

\* Mechanism: a bounded work queue admits containers under backpressure; a
\* crane then books queued containers into free slots in FIFO order and
\* releases the longest-held slot first. Capacity can be widened or
\* narrowed by ChangeCapacity at any time.

Init ==
  /\ capacity \in MinCap..MaxCap
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ assignedList = <<>>
  /\ free = [s \in Slots |-> TRUE]
  /\ nextJob = 1
  /\ serviced = {}

Enqueue ==
  /\ nextJob <= MaxJobs
  /\ Len(queue) < capacity
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, nextJob)
  /\ nextJob' = nextJob + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, assignedList, free, serviced>>

ChangeCapacity ==
  \E c \in MinCap..MaxCap :
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, assignedList, free, nextJob, serviced>>

Allocate ==
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ \E s \in Slots :
       /\ free[s]
       /\ assignedList' = Append(assignedList, <<s, Head(queue)>>)
       /\ free' = [free EXCEPT ![s] = FALSE]
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, nextJob, serviced>>

Release ==
  /\ assignedList # <<>>
  /\ LET pair == Head(assignedList)
         s    == pair[1]
         j    == pair[2]
     IN /\ assignedList' = Tail(assignedList)
        /\ free' = [free EXCEPT ![s] = TRUE]
        /\ serviced' = serviced \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, queue, nextJob>>

Next == Enqueue \/ ChangeCapacity \/ Allocate \/ Release

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ SF_vars(Allocate) /\ SF_vars(Release)

\* Safety: the cached free-slot flags must always agree with the ordered
\* occupancy record, so a slot's cache can never claim "free" while the
\* record still lists it held (which is what would let a second container
\* be booked onto a still-occupied slot).
FreeFlagsCoherent ==
  \A s \in Slots :
    free[s] <=> (\A i \in DOMAIN assignedList : assignedList[i][1] # s)

\* Liveness: any container that ever entered the queue must eventually be
\* marked serviced, not merely allocated then forgotten.
EventualService == \A j \in Jobs : (j < nextJob) ~> (j \in serviced)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
  Slots = {1, 2}
  MinCap = 1
  MaxCap = 2
  MaxJobs = 3

INVARIANT FreeFlagsCoherent
PROPERTY EventualService
nl:
A container-ship crane yard manages incoming containers destined for a small
fixed set of storage slots on the quay. Arriving containers are admitted into
a bounded work queue that a dispatcher maintains; the queue enforces
backpressure by refusing to admit a new container whenever it is already
holding as many containers as the queue's current capacity allows. Yard
operators can change that capacity at runtime -- widening it during a lull to
let more containers wait, or narrowing it during congestion -- and every
future admission decision immediately respects the new limit. A crane
repeatedly pulls the oldest waiting container from the queue and books it
into any storage slot that is currently free, updating both the crane's
ordered slot-occupancy record and its cached free-slot flags together in the
same step. Once a container has finished being handled, the crane releases
the container that has been holding a slot the longest, marks that container
as serviced, and flips its slot's cached flag back to free. SAFETY PROPERTY:
the crane's cached free-slot flags always agree exactly with which slots
actually appear in the active slot-occupancy record, so no slot can ever be
booked to a second container while the record still shows it held by a
first. LIVENESS PROPERTY: every container admitted into the queue is
eventually marked serviced.
